newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo to insist on barcoded freight ship.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo to insist on barcoded freight ship.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG will refuse air cargo shipments without barcode stickers from April 1998 under its new quality drive, senior officials said.
Stefan Lauer, the airline's board member for sales and marketing, told a meeting with 50 leading freight forwarders that barcoding would be the basis of a worldwide tracking and tracing system.

But Lufthansa Cargo needed the support of freight forwarders, who accounted for 80 percent of the airline's sales revenue, to introduce a functioning system, he said at the meeting organised by the German forwarders association BSL.
Lauer stressed Lufthansa and forwarders should concentrate on their core business but should increase joint marketing of air cargo services to shippers, a BSL statement said.
Silke Lehnhardt, the airline's cargo strategies implementation manager, said barcoding was an essential part of improving the quality of air cargo transport.
In a six-month test phase starting this summer, all shipments from Germany should be labelled with barcodes with Lufthansa adding stickers to non-labelled goods, she added.
From the start of 1998, all shipments worldwide should be labelled and Lufthansa will have introduced scanning equipment at all major stations.

From next April, Lufthansa Cargo would only accept barcoded shipments with forwarders able to buy stickers from the airline if necessary, Lehnhardt said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017 - www.racs.com
